```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
# devtools::install_github("mkim425/modelimportance")
library(modelimportance)
# install.packages("hubVis", repos = c("https://hubverse-org.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

library(ggplot2)
library(here)
setwd(here())
```

We explore the robustness of model importance using the leave-one-model-out (LOMO) approach 
on the case study of 4-week ahead incident death forecasts in Massachusetts (MA).

## Variance of importance scores for the case study

```{r varaince_importance_scores}
# Load data of importance scores
forecast_ma2021_full <- readRDS("../Data/forecast_death_ma2021.rds")

# Calculate variance of importance scores for each target_end_date
forecast_ma2021_full |>
  filter(!grepl("Ens", model)) |>
  group_by(target_end_date) |>
  summarize(variance = var(importance)) |>
  filter(variance == max(variance) | variance == min(variance))
```

The least variable importance scores are observed for the target end date "2021-07-24", 
while the most variable importance scores are observed for the target end date "2021-08-28".


## Load data for specific prediction tasks

Now we load the forecast data and truth data for these specific prediction tasks, and 
convert them to the required format for the `model_importance()` function.

```{r load_data_specific_tasks}
# Load forecast data
forecasts_MA_2021 <- read.csv("../Data/forecasts_MA_2021_hor1-4.csv")
forecasts_MA_2021$target_end_date <- as.Date(forecasts_MA_2021$target_end_date)

truth <- read.csv("../Data/truth_MA_2021.csv") |>
  select(target_end_date, location, value) |>
  mutate(
    target_end_date = as.Date(target_end_date),
    target = "wk inc death"
  ) |>
  rename(oracle_value = value)

# forecast data for MA, 4-week ahead incident death (horizon = 4)
# target_end_date = "2021-07-24",
models2include <- c(
  "CovidAnalytics-DELPHI", "USC-SI_kJalpha",
  "BPagano-RtDriven", "Karlen-pypm",
  "SteveMcConnell-CovidComplete", "UMass-MechBayes",
  "RobertWalraven-ESG", "COVIDhub-baseline",
  "UCSD_NEU-DeepGLEAM"
)

fdat <- forecasts_MA_2021 |>
  filter(
    model %in% models2include,
    location == "25",
    horizon == 4
  ) |>
  mutate(
    target = "wk inc death"
  ) |>
  rename(
    model_id = model,
    reference_date = forecast_date,
    output_type = type,
    output_type_id = quantile
  ) |>
  select(
    model_id, reference_date, location, horizon,
    target_end_date, target, output_type,
    output_type_id, value
  )

fdat0724 <- fdat |>
  filter(target_end_date == as.Date("2021-07-24")) |>
  mutate(reference_date = as.Date("2021-06-28"))

fdat0828 <- fdat |>
  filter(target_end_date == as.Date("2021-08-28")) |>
  mutate(reference_date = as.Date("2021-08-02"))
```

## Variability analysis 

First, we store the importance score using all 9 models as a reference.
```{r importance_ref_scores}
# Reference importance scores for the two target end dates
imp_ref <- forecast_ma2021_full |>
  filter(
    !grepl("Ens", model),
    target_end_date %in% c(as.Date("2021-07-24"), as.Date("2021-08-28"))
  ) |>  
        rename(model_id = model) |>
  select(model_id, target_end_date)
```


Next, we calculate importance scores using the LOMO approach for each subset of models.
For this calculation, we use the `model_importance()` function from the `modelimportance` package.
The output is a data frame with columns `model_id, mean_importance, excluded_model` per each excluded model:

- `model_id`: the ID of the model whose importance score is calculated
- `mean_importance`: the importance score of the model. Since we have only one prediction task, this is the same as the importance score.
- `excluded_model`: the ID of the model that was excluded when calculating the importance score.
- `target_end_date`: the target end date for which the importance score is calculated.

Note that the excluded model's importance metric is assigned as NA.


### Target end date: 2021-07-24 (least variable importance scores)

```{r importance_lomo_0724}
models <- unique(fdat$model_id)

results_df <- list()
for (i in 2:9) {
  combo_list <- combn(models, i, simplify = FALSE)
  results_df[[i]] <- furrr::future_map_dfr(
    combo_list,
    function(combo) {
      dat <- fdat0724 |> filter(model_id %in% combo)

      res <- suppressMessages(
        model_importance(
          forecast_data = dat,
          oracle_output_data = truth,
          ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
          weighted = FALSE,
          importance_algorithm = "lomo"
        ) |>
          mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))
      ) |>
        right_join(imp_ref |> filter(target_end_date == "2021-07-24"), 
                   by = "model_id") |>
        arrange(model_id) |>
        mutate(
          subset_size = length(combo),
          included_models = paste(combo, collapse = ", ")
        )

      res
    }
  )
}

all_dfs0724 <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_df)
```


```{r plot_importance_0724}
model_sorted <- imp_ref |> 
        arrange(model_id) |> 
        pull(model_id) |> unique()

data2plot <- all_dfs0724 |> 
  mutate(model_id = factor(model_id, levels = model_sorted)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_importance)) 

# Plot importance distributions across different subset sizes
p0724 <- data2plot |> 
        filter(subset_size < 9) |> 
        ggplot(aes(x = factor(subset_size), y = mean_importance)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2), alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
        stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", color = "blue", size = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ model_id, scales = "free_y") +
  geom_point(
    data = data2plot |> 
        filter(subset_size == 9),
    mapping = aes(x = factor(subset_size), y = mean_importance), size = 1) +
        labs(#title = "Model importance metric distributions across different subset sizes \n(Target end date: 2021-07-24)",
             x = "Number of models in the subset",
             y = "Importance") + 
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=9),
              axis.title=element_text(size=11),
              legend.position = "none",
              strip.text = element_text(size = 10))
```

## Investigate subset weights in LASOMO and their impact on importance scores

We further investigate the subset weights in the LASOMO approach and their impact on importance scores.
```{r}
df_karlen <- all_dfs0828 |> 
        filter(model_id == "Karlen-pypm", !is.na(mean_importance)) |> 
        mutate(S_size = subset_size -1) |> # S: subset without the target model as in the Shapley value formula
        select(-included_models, -target_end_date)
``` 

```{r}
df_karlen_wt_cal <- df_karlen |> 
  mutate(
          wt_perm = 1 / ((n - 1) * choose(n - 1, S_size)),
          wt_eq = 1 / (2^(n - 1) - 1)
          )

summary <- df_karlen_wt_cal |> 
        group_by(subset_size, S_size) |> 
        summarize(
          mean_imp = mean(mean_importance),
          n= n(), 
          wt_perm = unique(wt_perm),
          wt_eq = unique(wt_eq),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) |> 
        mutate(
          wt_perm_n = n * wt_perm,
          wt_eq_n = n * wt_eq,
          imp_wt_perm = mean_imp * wt_perm_n,
          imp_wt_eq = mean_imp * wt_eq_n
        ) 


summary |> 
        summarize(
          imp_lasomo_avg_mean_imp = mean(mean_imp),
          imp_lasomo_perm = sum(imp_wt_perm),
          imp_lasomo_eq = sum(imp_wt_eq)
        )
```



```{r}
suppressMessages(
        model_importance(
          forecast_data = fdat0828,
          oracle_output_data = truth,
          ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
          weighted = FALSE,
          importance_algorithm = "lasomo",
          subset_wt = "perm_based"
        )
        )|> 
        filter(model_id == "Karlen-pypm")
```

```{r}
suppressMessages(
        model_importance(
          forecast_data = fdat0828,
          oracle_output_data = truth,
          ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
          weighted = FALSE,
          importance_algorithm = "lasomo",
          subset_wt = "equal"
        )) |> 
        filter(model_id == "Karlen-pypm")
```

## Prediction plot of the forecasts via hubVis

```{r warning=FALSE}
target_data1 <- truth |> 
        filter(target_end_date <= as.Date("2021-06-26"),
               target_end_date >= as.Date("2021-04-15")) |> 
        rename(date = target_end_date,
               observation = oracle_value)
model_out_tbl1 <- fdat |> 
        filter(target_end_date >= as.Date("2021-06-20"),
               target_end_date <= as.Date("2021-07-30")) |> 
        rename(target_date = target_end_date) 
p1 <- plot_step_ahead_model_output(model_out_tbl1, target_data1, 
                             use_median_as_point = TRUE,
                             pal_color = "Paired",
                             show_legend = FALSE,
                             interactive = FALSE, 
                             facet = "model_id") + 
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=9),
              axis.title=element_text(size=11),
              strip.text = element_text(size = 10))

```
